checkpoint.selection: earliest head containing the escaped defect

entries.statement: NewNodeManager returns an error when NodeIPs cannot be retrieved within the poll window, and newProxyServer propagates it, aborting kube-proxy startup. The replaced code was non-fatal: it returned possibly-empty IPs and detectNodeIPs fell back to localhost/BindAddress, letting kube-proxy start degraded.
entries.locus: newNodeManager poll -> `return nil, err` (node.go:95); propagated at cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:227-229
entries.source_ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132958 (revert), /133059 (take 2); foreshadowed pre-merge by danwinship thread on server.go:705, 2025-03-15
entries.admission_evidence: Present at checkpoint. Verified in the fixture: node.go:49 `NewNodeManager(...) (*NodeManager, error)`, node.go:95 `return nil, err`, server.go:229 `return nil, err` propagating it. Absent at pushes #0/#1, where NewNodeManager returned `*NodeManager` with no error path.
entries.must_flag: Flags that failure to obtain NodeIPs now ABORTS kube-proxy startup where the previous behavior was non-fatal with a localhost/BindAddress fallback. Equivalent framings count ('kube-proxy will fail to start if the node has no IPs yet', 'this should degrade rather than error', 'breaks cloud-provider startup ordering'). Merely noting that a timeout exists, or praising it, does NOT count.
entries.must_not_require: Do NOT require the reviewer to mention a 5-minute timeout. At this checkpoint the poll timeout is 30s (node.go:50, `30*time.Second`); the widening to 5 minutes came later. Only the fatal-vs-non-fatal claim is in scope here.

entries.statement: All NodeManager exit paths call plain klog.Flush() followed by exitFunc(1) instead of the codebase-standard klog.FlushAndExit(klog.ExitFlushTimeout, 1). Plain Flush() is synchronous and unbounded, so a stalled log sink can prevent the exit from being reached, and buffered logs explaining the crash can be lost.
entries.source_ref: nojnhuh, PR thread 2025-07-15: 'this PR seems to have broken creating clusters for me... previous klog.FlushAndExit() may have been more robust'
entries.admission_evidence: Present at checkpoint. Verified: 3 occurrences of `klog.Flush()` + `n.exitFunc(1)` at node.go:132/148/156, 0 occurrences of klog.FlushAndExit. Pushes #0/#1 had 2x klog.FlushAndExit and 0 plain Flush(), so the defect entered at this checkpoint.
entries.must_flag: Flags that the exit paths use unbounded klog.Flush() rather than the bounded klog.FlushAndExit, risking lost crash diagnostics or a hung exit.
